title: The big ph site of schemes
statement: Fix the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ be the category of schemes in the chosen universe over $S$, with all $S$-morphisms. Its ph topology is the smallest Grothendieck topology [def-weil-pbc-topos] containing the sieves generated by the Zariski covering families (families $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ of open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] whose images cover $T$) and by every singleton $\{V\to T\}$ that is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and surjective (surjective on underlying points). Write $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_{ph}$ for this big site, using an admissible small presentation in a larger universe, and $\mathrm{Sh}((\mathrm{Sch}/S)_{ph})$ for its sheaf topos [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

I also read all five cited dependencies, the unit sk-i-curve-zero and the chapter, and the three citers (proper-hypercover-etale-descent, simplicial-ph-etale-square, ph-etale-torsion-comparison). The statement is correct. The smallest Grothendieck topology containing the sieves of Zariski covers and of singleton proper surjections equals the topology of Stacks' ph coverings. One direction: both kinds of generator are ph coverings (0DBH, surjective-proper-ph), and ph coverings satisfy the site axioms (0DBI). The other direction: a standard ph covering's sieve is a J-sieve by transitivity, applied to the proper surjection followed by an affine Zariski cover, and local character finishes it. So the two topologies have the same sheaves, as 0DBQ says. Edge cases checked: a surjection that is not of finite type, such as Spec k-bar over Spec k, is not a covering; T_red into T is a covering; the empty cover; the size choice of all U-schemes is admissible. A grep of the DAG for ph and 0DB* tags found no duplicate. The item has no new nodes or proof steps, and no tool_uses. Three small repairs are in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/def-trf-ph-scheme-site.json.
